minutes.headline: Commission cut a lake homeowner's tree replacement from six trees to mountain laurel and blueberry shrubs, 4-1.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard a field change request at 16 Roof Street, approving shrubs (mountain laurel and blueberry) in place of required replacement trees, with one member dissenting. Most public hearings were continued to August 18th or September 1st. The members also discussed a tree definition, a hay field license, possible encroachments on conservation land, and the 40B proposal at 318 Howard Street. Minutes of July 21st were approved as amended.

Andrea Adams asked about the rebuilt Pleasant Street bridge over Pearl Brook, which has a deck and guardrail but no walls closing the gap, and was told the commission's agent would check on it after vacation.

A member asked who pays if a neighbor disputes a property line and the town must fund a survey. The chair said he would ask town counsel.

decisions.decision: The commission's agent will issue an amended order of conditions for 16 Roof Street after reviewing the meeting.
The land use management plan update (removing the bow hunting special permit) was continued to the next meeting, since the advertisement named the 18th.
Jack Rabbit will red-line the wetlands regulations to add a tree definition, and the chair wants every use of 'tree' reviewed. Any change needs two televised public hearings.
The commission agreed to take ground-level photographs of possible encroachments before asking town counsel to send letters, and to seek a volunteer with a drone.
No special meeting will be called for the 40B response. Members were told to send individual concerns to the town by the deadline.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved, 4-1, a field change at 16 Roof Street that replaces required trees with mountain laurel and blueberry shrubs.
An amendment to add two trees to the open area at 16 Roof Street failed for lack of a second.
Four hearings were continued to August 18th and one to September 1st, each by roll call.
The commission authorized the chair to ask town counsel to draft a license for haying the Pleasant Street hay field, for the commission to review first.

Members agreed to photograph possible encroachments on conservation land from the ground before asking town counsel to send letters, and declined to call a special meeting on the 40B at 318 Howard Street.

why_it_matters: The Roof Street vote shows how the commission treats a tree-replacement requirement at the water's edge, and a change to the wetlands regulations' tree definition would apply to future applicants.
The hay field license and the encroachment letters bear on how town-owned conservation land is used and protected, and who pays if a boundary survey is needed is still unanswered.
The 40B proposal at 318 Howard Street will go to the state with comments from individual members rather than a commission position.
watch_next: The August 18th meeting, where most continued hearings and the land use management plan update (bow hunting permit) are due.
Jack Rabbit's red-lined tree definition, which would need two televised public hearings before any change.
